Riyadh — Saudi proptech startup Ghanem has successfully raised $7.1 million from the Al-Romaih Group to accelerate the development and expansion of its digital fractional real estate ownership platform. Founded in 2025 by Saleh Al-Ghamdi and Amr Essam, Ghanem operates within the Regulatory Sandbox of the Saudi Real Estate General Authority (REGA). The capital injection aims to lower the entry barriers for individual and institutional investors in the Saudi real estate market, providing them with transparent and flexible investment opportunities. This move aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 objectives of digital transformation and real estate diversification.

The digital fractional real estate ownership model specializes in dividing property assets into smaller, accessible shares. This structure lowers the entry thresholds for investors who previously faced significant capital requirements in the traditional real estate market. Ghanem's platform focuses on offering transparency and flexibility, which are core components of its strategy to attract a broader base of participants to the property sector. The newly acquired capital from the Al-Romaih Group will be directed toward accelerating product development and expanding the platform's market presence across the region.

Operating under the Regulatory Sandbox of the Real Estate General Authority allows Ghanem to test its digital fractional ownership model within a structured environment. The REGA framework provides oversight while the startup develops its product offerings. Saleh Al-Ghamdi and Amr Essam established the company to address the demand for alternative investment structures in the real estate sector. The $7.1 million investment provides the financial resources necessary to refine the platform's features and increase its operational capacity.
